paragraphs.title: The Purpose of Proverbs and the Foundation of Wisdom

answers: The father of the young man
easy.explanation: Verse 1 identifies the proverbs as those of Solomon the son of David, king of Israel.
easy.q: Who is identified as the author of the proverbs at the beginning of the chapter?

easy.explanation: The opening verses say the proverbs are given to know wisdom and instruction.
easy.q: What are the proverbs intended to provide?

easy.explanation: Verse 7 states, “The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.”
easy.q: What is the beginning of knowledge according to the passage?

answers: Wisdom includes instruction in justice, judgment, and equity
Wisdom is intended only for kings
medium.explanation: The passage connects wisdom with instruction, justice, judgment, equity, knowledge, and discretion.
medium.q: How does the passage connect wisdom with practical understanding?

medium.explanation: Wise counsels are sound advice or guidance.
medium.q: In the phrase “a man of understanding shall attain unto wise counsels,” what does “counsels” mean?

medium.explanation: Verse 5 says, “A wise man will hear, and will increase learning.”
medium.q: What will a wise man do according to verse 5?

answers: Wisdom is only for people who are already wise
Wisdom can benefit people at different levels of understanding
challenge.explanation: The passage mentions the simple, the young, the wise, and the understanding, showing that wisdom can benefit many kinds of people.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from the book addressing both the simple and the wise?

answers: The fear of the LORD and fools who despise wisdom and instruction
challenge.explanation: The fear of the LORD is called the beginning of knowledge, while fools despise wisdom and instruction.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast in verse 7?

challenge.explanation: Verse 1 identifies Solomon as the king of Israel and the source of the proverbs.
challenge.q: According to verse 1, who was the king of Israel named as the source of these proverbs?

easy.explanation: The father is speaking directly to his son.
easy.q: To whom does the phrase “My son” refer?

easy.explanation: Verse 8 says, “My son, hear the instruction of thy father.”
easy.q: What is the son told to hear?

easy.explanation: The verse says, “forsake not the law of thy mother.”
easy.q: What is the son told not to forsake?

answers: As an ornament and chains that bring honor
medium.explanation: They are described as an ornament of grace to the head and chains about the neck.
medium.q: How are the father's instruction and the mother's law described?

answers: Parental instruction adds grace and honor to a person
Obedience prevents a person from learning
medium.explanation: The ornament imagery presents good instruction as something beautiful and honorable.
medium.q: What relationship does the passage suggest between obeying parents and the ornament imagery?

medium.explanation: To forsake something means to abandon or leave it.
medium.q: In the phrase “forsake not the law of thy mother,” what does “forsake” mean?

answers: Instruction in the home is presented as coming from both parents
Only the father is responsible for teaching
Only the mother is responsible for teaching
challenge.explanation: The passage names both the father's instruction and the mother's law.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from mentioning both the father and the mother?

answers: It shows that instruction adds grace, beauty, and honor
It shows that instruction is dangerous
It shows that instruction is a form of spoil
challenge.explanation: The comparisons portray parental instruction as something valuable and honorable.
challenge.q: Why is instruction compared with an ornament and chains?

answers: The son first rejects his parents and then accepts their advice
The son is told to listen and not forsake instruction, and then its benefit is described
The son is first taught robbery and then wisdom
challenge.explanation: Verse 8 gives the command, and verse 9 describes the honor that follows.
challenge.q: What is the logical order of these two verses?

paragraphs.title: The Sinners' Temptation and the Trap of Crime

easy.explanation: They tempt him to come with them and participate in their plans.
easy.q: What do sinners urge the young man to do?

easy.explanation: They plan to lie in wait for blood and the innocent without cause.
easy.q: Whom do the sinners plan to attack?

easy.explanation: They say, “we shall fill our houses with spoil.”
easy.q: What do they promise to fill their houses with?

answers: Their feet run to evil and hasten to shed blood
medium.explanation: The passage says their feet run to evil and make haste to shed blood.
medium.q: Why does the father warn the son not to walk with the sinners?

answers: A person who has done no wrong
medium.explanation: The innocent are people who have done nothing deserving of attack.
medium.q: In the phrase “the innocent without cause,” what does “innocent” mean?

answers: A danger that can trap those who set it
medium.explanation: The image warns that those who prepare traps for others may bring danger upon themselves.
medium.q: What does the net spread before a bird illustrate?

answers: Greed can ultimately harm the greedy person
challenge.explanation: Verse 19 says the way of the greedy takes away the life of its owners.
challenge.q: What is the central lesson at the end of this passage?

answers: As an invitation to share in violence and spoil
As an invitation to study wisdom
challenge.explanation: They invite the young man to join them, share their lot, and divide the spoil.
challenge.q: How is the sinners' temptation presented?

challenge.explanation: They say, “let us all have one purse.”
challenge.q: What do the sinners propose that everyone should have together, according to verse 14?

easy.explanation: Verse 20 says, “Wisdom crieth without; she uttereth her voice in the streets.”
Wisdom addresses the simple ones, the scorners, and fools.
She promises, “I will pour out my spirit unto you, I will make known my words unto you.”
easy.q: What does wisdom promise to those who turn at her reproof?

answers: She is accessible to the public
She is intended only for hidden people
She is given to only one person
medium.explanation: Wisdom calls in the streets, public gathering places, and city gates.
medium.q: What does the public setting of wisdom's call suggest about her availability?

medium.explanation: “Crieth” means calls out or cries aloud.
medium.q: In the phrase “Wisdom crieth without,” what does “crieth” mean?

medium.explanation: Wisdom says, “Turn you at my reproof,” before promising further instruction.
medium.q: What is required before wisdom will make her words known?

answers: To emphasize that her guidance is open and available
To invite people to commit crimes
challenge.explanation: Her public call shows that wisdom is not secret or restricted to a select group.
challenge.q: Why is wisdom portrayed as calling aloud?

answers: Wisdom offers correction even to those who resist or despise it
challenge.explanation: Wisdom calls even those who reject knowledge and invites them to turn.
challenge.q: What can be inferred from wisdom addressing both scorners and fools?

answers: Accepting correction opens the way to further instruction
The words are given only after a crime
challenge.explanation: Wisdom promises to make her words known to those who turn at her reproof.
challenge.q: What is the relationship between turning at reproof and receiving wisdom's words?

answers: They refused and did not regard her
easy.explanation: They refused wisdom's call, disregarded her outstretched hand, and rejected her counsel.
easy.q: How did the people respond when wisdom called?

easy.explanation: Verse 28 says, “Then shall they call upon me, but I will not answer.”
easy.q: What will happen when fear and destruction come upon them?

answers: He shall fill his house with spoil
easy.explanation: The final verse says, “whoso hearkeneth unto me shall dwell safely.”
easy.q: What is promised to the person who listens to wisdom?

answers: They previously rejected her counsel and reproof
medium.explanation: Their later distress follows their earlier refusal to accept wisdom's counsel.
medium.q: Why will wisdom not answer them in their trouble?

medium.explanation: Here prosperity refers to the fools' ease or apparent success, which ultimately destroys them.
medium.q: In the phrase “the prosperity of fools,” what does “prosperity” most nearly mean?

answers: People will eat the fruit of their own way and be filled with their own devices
People always receive the opposite of what they do
A person's way has no effect on the result
medium.explanation: The verse teaches that people experience the consequences of their chosen way and devices.
medium.q: What cause-and-effect relationship is stated in verse 31?

answers: Those who reject wisdom suffer, while those who listen dwell safely
challenge.explanation: The passage contrasts the destruction of those who reject wisdom with the safety of those who hear her.
challenge.q: What is the main contrast at the end of the passage?

answers: They will experience the results of their choices
Wisdom will provide them with food
challenge.explanation: The phrase means that people will receive the consequences produced by their own conduct.
challenge.q: What does “they shall eat of the fruit of their own way” mean in context?

challenge.explanation: Verse 33 says the one who hearkens to wisdom “shall be quiet from fear of evil.”
challenge.q: According to the final verse, what will the person who listens to wisdom be quiet from?
